sources.title: Sync your Lovable project with GitHub
sources.note: Lovable syncs one active branch at a time. Changes on that branch sync in both directions. Connecting creates a private repository by default. Transferring the repository or renaming the owner breaks sync; repository renames are tracked.

sources.title: Deploying Git Repositories with Vercel
sources.note: Branch pushes create previews and production-branch changes create production deployments.

sources.title: Deploying GitHub Projects with Vercel
sources.note: Vercel posts preview deployments for pull requests and protects fork previews from unapproved access to deployment secrets.

sources.title: Environments
sources.note: Vercel provides Local, Preview and Production environments; environment-specific behavior must be verified separately.

sources.title: Deployment Checks
sources.note: Where available, deployment checks can gate production promotion on selected GitHub checks. The release must not assume plan availability.

sources.title: Rolling back a production deployment
sources.note: Vercel can reassign production traffic to an earlier deployment, but code rollback does not reverse browser-side data migrations.

sources.title: Promoting a preview deployment to production
sources.note: Promotion rebuilds with production environment variables, so production must be rechecked even after preview passes.

sources.title: Setting up a custom domain
sources.note: Inspect the exact DNS records shown for the project; Vercel provisions TLS after verification.

sources.title: Environment variables
sources.note: Variables can differ across Development, Preview and Production. This local-first app should have no secrets unless a later approved feature requires them.

sources.title: About protected branches
sources.note: Required status checks can prevent merges until checks pass. Feature availability depends on repository visibility and account plan.

sources.title: Dependabot quickstart guide
sources.note: Dependabot alerts, security updates and version updates are distinct capabilities.

sources.title: Configuring default setup for code scanning
sources.note: Code scanning availability depends on repository visibility and GitHub plan. It is conditional, not a universal release gate.

sources.title: actions/setup-node
sources.note: Specify the project Node version, commit the package-manager lockfile and use the immutable CI install command for the detected package manager.

sources.title: Testing overview
sources.note: Test-tool choice must follow the actual Lovable scaffold; do not migrate the framework for this phase.

sources.title: Testing with Vitest
sources.note: Vitest and Testing Library are suitable when compatible with the actual scaffold; async server behavior requires browser-level coverage where unit support is incomplete.

sources.title: React Testing Library
sources.note: Tests should interact with accessible DOM behavior instead of component implementation details.

sources.title: Coverage
sources.note: Coverage is a diagnostic and release input, not proof of correctness. Critical calculation and migration code receives stricter coverage than ordinary presentation code.

sources.title: Testing with Playwright
sources.note: Run browser tests against a production-like build and cover real navigation and persistence flows.

sources.title: Playwright projects
sources.note: Projects can run the same tests across Chromium, Firefox, WebKit and emulated devices.

sources.title: Continuous Integration
sources.note: CI must install browser dependencies and retain traces/reports only when they contain synthetic test data.

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2
sources.note: WCAG conformance requires automated and human evaluation; automated tools alone cannot prove conformance.

sources.title: axe-core
sources.note: Automated accessibility testing finds a subset of issues; manual keyboard, zoom, screen-reader and cognitive review remains required.

sources.title: Production checklist
sources.note: The actual framework may differ; apply equivalent production checks without migrating scaffolds.

sources.title: Content Security Policy
sources.note: CSP must be tested against the actual rendering mode and approved external resources; do not copy a nonce-based pattern into a static app blindly.

sources.title: Lighthouse CI
sources.note: Use lab audits and budgets as regression controls; they are not production field data.

sources.title: Web Vitals
sources.note: LCP, INP and CLS are field metrics with recommended thresholds. Without privacy-approved field telemetry, the app must not claim production CWV compliance from Lighthouse alone.

testSuites.name: Repository contract
checks: one supported package manager and lockfile
no generated secrets or personal data

testSuites.name: Formatting and lint
checks: no ignored errors without documented waiver

testSuites.name: Privacy and network audit
checks: external embeds are user-triggered where required

testSuites.name: Performance regression
checks: no blocking index work on main thread

releaseGates.name: Formatting, lint and strict typecheck pass
All static data and relationships validate
Critical formulas, migrations and export logic pass
Critical E2E journeys pass on required browsers
Automated checks and manual release review pass
No personal data leaves the browser
No unresolved release-blocking secret, CSP or dependency issue
Backup, restore, migration and rollback compatibility pass
Canonical production domain and TLS are valid
Release manifest and changelog are complete
Owner creates an external Phase 17 backup before first production upgrade with schema changes
Production smoke checks pass after release

vercelEnvironments.purpose: Local development against synthetic data; no production personal data.
Every branch and pull request; full smoke and visual acceptance without touching the production origin.
Canonical custom domain; real personal data may exist only after Phase 17 backup and restore are verified.

originContinuityRules: Choose one canonical custom production domain before using real personal records.
Redirect alternate hostnames to the canonical host; do not use both as separate app origins.
Changing domain, protocol or port creates a different browser-storage origin.
To move origins: export from the old origin, verify the file, open the new origin, preview restore, then restore.
Never delete or detach the old origin until the migrated backup is verified on the new origin.

dataCompatibilityPolicy.previousReleaseCompatibility: test at least the immediately previous production version against the candidate database state
dataCompatibilityPolicy.rollbackRule: Vercel code rollback is allowed only when the target code can read the current local data schema. Otherwise ship a forward fix.

integrityTests.expect: CI detects the actual package manager, lockfile, framework and runtime before generating workflows.
Phase 18 does not migrate the Lovable-native framework.
CI uses the immutable install command and fails if the lockfile is inconsistent.
All automated fixtures and uploaded artifacts contain synthetic records only.
Every public and personal-data schema test passes without converting missing values to zero.
Candidate code reads a database produced by the previous production version.
Previous production code is tested against the candidate-migrated database before declaring rollback safe.
Quota errors preserve existing data and produce a recoverable UI state.
Restore preview performs zero canonical writes.
The runbook does not claim automatic browser-data transfer across origins.
No personal field appears in captured network requests.
No analytics SDK exists unless separately approved and documented.
Release cannot claim WCAG compliance solely from axe or Lighthouse.
Release includes manual smoke on one real iOS and one real Android device.
Every feature release is verified on a Vercel preview before main is merged.
Production is rechecked because production environment variables and origin differ from preview.
Canonical domain, redirects and TLS pass before real personal use.
GitHub Actions workflows use least-privilege permissions and no write token on untrusted PR code.
Third-party actions are pinned according to repository policy and updated through reviewed Dependabot PRs.
Dependency alerts are enabled; version-update cadence is documented.
CodeQL is required only where repository visibility and plan support it.
Every production release records commit, app version, content versions, schema compatibility and deployment URL.
Rollback runbook distinguishes code rollback, data recovery and origin migration.
CI artifacts never include real personal data or backup files.
A fresh clone can install, validate, test and build without Lovable access.
Deployment does not depend on Lovable runtime services or hidden cloud resources.
Official source URLs and review dates are stored in the Phase 18 reference package.
Lighthouse lab scores are not described as production Core Web Vitals field compliance.
A failed required check cannot be documented as release-ready.
Owner can restore from GitHub, Vercel history and a Phase 17 data backup using written runbooks.
